newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine T-bill payments delayed half a day-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine T-bill payments delayed half a day-dealers.

text.p: Ukraine's Finance Ministry was half a day late paying 4.07 trillion karbovanets in interest and principal on three issues of Treasury bills, dealers said on Thursday.
"The money arrived only today at 11:44 in the morning, but was supposed to be here by the end of the day yesterday," dealer Alexei Molotkovich of Mriya bank told Reuters.
A finance ministry official blamed the delay on late payments by banks for T-bills purchased earlier in the week.

"The commercial banks were supposed to have paid for the T-bills no later than 6 p.m. on Wednesday, but we did not receive the money in the full amount," said Leonid Kuchyn, deputy head of the ministry's accounts department.
Alexander Parshakov, managing partner of Finance and Credit Invest, said the delay would damage the market.
"They have to understand that if they want to be successful in the market they have to pay at the moment they say they'll pay," Parshakov said.
"I would be very much surprised if the U.S. government delayed payments by a day," said Parshakov, whose company recently published a guide to investing in Ukraine's T-bills.

Ukraine's T-bill market, which is about 18-months-old, has attracted mainly local buyers and only a small number of foreigners. Many potential foreign investors have been deterred by unclear tax rules on profits from the bills.
National Bank of Ukraine officials said they were given no explanation for the delayed payments.
Since 1995, when T-bills were first issued, the ministry has been late in paying by a couple of hours only twice, a ministry official said.
Under ministry-central bank agreements the government is required to pay a 0.05 percent fine for every day of delay. --Natalia Zinets, Kiev Newsroom, +380 44 229 2264
